analyst_view.overall: Werder Bremen (6th, 18 points, unbeaten in five home games) host bottom side Gladbach (4 points from 10) on Friday night, five days after a 4-0 Nordderby win over Hamburg and a new contract for coach Daniel Thioune. Werder's attack has fresh question marks: two-goal derby hero Justin Njinmah has muscle problems (BILD via Head Topics, and Ligainsider lists him as knocked), Marco Grull is still in rehab with a calf injury, Mitchell Weiser's return is likely but not certain, and Senne Lynen is back in training after illness; Agu, Stage, Musah, Topp and N'Diaye stay out. For Gladbach, Tim Kleindienst and Hugo Bolin returned to training on Monday but Alexander Blessin says he will not rush them, and Robin Hack missed training with a muscle problem. The numbers already take off Weiser, Bolin and Ullrich and add for Werder's strong recent shooting and Gladbach's high card count, but they do not know about Grull, Njinmah or Hack, so I trim goals, shots and shots on target a little. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.9 for Werder, and already take off Weiser (who now looks likely to play, a small plus) and Bolin and Ullrich for Gladbach. What they do not see is that Grull, Werder's top creator, is still in rehab, Njinmah, who scored twice against Hamburg, is carrying a muscle problem, and Hack, one of Gladbach's few attacking threats, missed training while Kleindienst is not ready to start. Together that pulls a little lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, 5.4 for Werder. Weiser's likely return gives Werder their usual width on the right, but Grull's absence and Agu still being out on the left take some crossing away; Gladbach's recent habit of conceding corners (37 in six) is already counted. These balance out, so I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Gladbach have collected 20 cards in their last six games, the sign of a side scrapping at the bottom, and the numbers already add about 8% for that; Werder's own card count has been low. No referee has been named and there is no derby edge, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, 18.3 for Werder, already boosted 11% for Werder's 105 shots in six games; Gladbach have lost five of seven away and will likely sit deep. With Grull out and Njinmah doubtful for Werder, and Hack doubtful for Gladbach, both sides may lose a few shots that Weiser's return only partly replaces, so I trim slightly to about 30.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, 7.0 for Werder, already boosted by Werder's sharp recent finishing (39 on target in six). Njinmah's muscle problem and Grull's absence take some of that sharpness away, and Gladbach's attack is thin without Kleindienst and with Hack doubtful, so I take a little off, to about 10.9.
